items.title: They Went to Ukraine on the ‘Peace Express.’ Detours Are Likely Ahead.
items.summary: The Trump administration had let the peace process enter such a freeze that a trip to Kyiv was just an initial step. Any new talks will happen alongside escalating fighting.

items.title: Israel Launches Deadly Strikes in Lebanon as Military Campaign Intensifies
items.summary: The bombardment killed 11 people, Lebanese officials said, after days of attacks that have spurred worries that Israel is looking to push deeper into Lebanese territory.

items.title: Germany’s ‘Firewall’ Against the Far Right Is Being Tested as Never Before
items.summary: A blowout win by the far-right Alternative for Germany party in a state election has revealed a split among voters about whether to uphold a decades-old strategy for sidelining extremists.

items.title: Britain Set to Target Israeli West Bank Settlements With Trade Ban
items.summary: The expected move will be announced on Tuesday, officials said, and underscored Israel’s mounting isolation over its policies toward Palestinians following the war in Gaza.

items.title: Canada’s Retaliatory Tariffs Set to Take Effect as Trump Threatens to Escalate
items.summary: New Canadian levies of up to 50 percent are expected to begin Tuesday, even as Washington warns of a new round of American tariffs.

items.title: Philippines Lawmaker, Cousin of Marcos, Charged With Taking Kickbacks
items.summary: A cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. was charged with plundering public funds meant for flood control in the Southeast Asian country. He has denied wrongdoing.

items.title: Thousands of Serbs Gather to Mourn Ratko Mladic, the ‘Butcher of Bosnia’
items.summary: The government insisted the funeral was a private affair, even as government ministers attended and state-controlled news media lavished praise on the convicted war criminal.

items.title: In Peru, the Trump Administration Sees the Limits of Its Anti-China Push
items.summary: As Secretary of State Marco Rubio travels this week to Peru, its growing economic ties to China have raised tensions with the U.S., but show no signs of reversing course.

items.title: After Victory in German State, Far Right Needs Help to Take Power
items.summary: The Alternative for Germany, or AfD, does not have a straightforward path to governing Saxony-Anhalt, but a small populist party could clear the way.

items.title: Germany’s Far Right Just Misses Majority in Crucial State Election
items.summary: The Alternative for Germany, or AfD, trounced its rivals but was left unsure if it will be able to govern in Saxony-Anhalt. The result shocked Germany.

items.title: WYouth, New Magazine for Teens, Debuts With Justin and Hailey Bieber Cover
items.summary: Sara Moonves managed to save and expand W, a fashion and culture magazine. Her next bet is on “Little W.”

items.title: Social Media in China Is Getting Really Dark
items.summary: The Chinese Communist Party has spent years trying to make “positive energy” the dominant mood of the country’s internet. It’s no longer working.

items.title: Rivian R2 Review: A Tidier (in Size and Price) SUV Is Ready for the Suburbs
items.summary: The electric automaker’s new R2 takes what works from its bigger, costlier brother and adds a host of features with the mass market in mind.

items.title: Oil Prices Rise After U.S. and Iran Trade Strikes
items.summary: Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil, rose to about $97 a barrel on Monday, while the national average price of gas was $4.15 a gallon.

items.title: Cargo Plane Crashes at Miami Airport, Striking Vehicles
items.summary: Officials said five others were injured. Flight disruptions at Miami International Airport continued on Monday morning.

items.title: OPEC Plus Holds Oil Production Steady as U.S.-Iran Strikes Resume
items.summary: The decision on Sunday by the cartel of oil-producing nations and some of its allies came after the resumption of U.S. and Iranian military strikes in the Persian Gulf.

items.title: Iran’s Attacks Keep the Strait of Hormuz in a Lethal Stalemate
items.summary: The U.S. military is helping oil get out of the Persian Gulf on tankers, but Iran is still attacking the ships and scaring operators away.

items.title: How a Blacklisted Chinese Tech Giant Kept Buying America’s Best A.I. Chips
items.summary: Washington imposed sanctions on Inspur because of its work with the Chinese military. But the company’s subsidiary kept shipping Nvidia’s best chips to feed China’s leading A.I. firms.

items.title: The C.E.O. Teaching Future Generations About 9/11
items.summary: Elizabeth Hillman, chief of the 9/11 Memorial & Museum since 2022, says the stories of that day “remain compelling, and they’re still unfolding.”

items.title: CCRCs Are Expanding Retirement Home Care to Seniors’ Own Homes
items.summary: Continuing care retirement communities are widening their scope to help retirees age in place, with measured supports and a way to cap the soaring costs of aging.

items.title: Kenyans Made a Living Writing College Essays. Then A.I. Arrived.
items.summary: Thousands of Kenyans made a living writing essays for overseas students. With A.I., the work has dried up, a warning for online gig work that has been a global lifeline.

items.title: Court Filings In A.I. Suit Invoke Copyright Law, Culture and Sports
items.summary: Filings made Friday in The New York Times’s closely watched lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft included a range of copyright law and cultural references.

items.title: Why the Hugging Face Hack Should Make You Worry More About A.I.
items.summary: The attack by an aggressive “collective” of OpenAI agents shows the danger of artificial intelligence systems that organize themselves.

items.title: Virtual Taekwondo Takes the Contact Out of a Combat Sport
items.summary: The contactless version of the Korean martial art is making its debut at this year’s Asian Games. Critics say it’s a glorified video game.

items.title: Early Data Indicates an A.I.-Generated Drug Could Slow Aging
items.summary: Artificial intelligence was used to help develop a drug candidate, rentosertib, for a rare lung condition. Its maker says the drug also seems to reduce the biological hallmarks of age.

items.title: Authors Wrangle With Publishers Over $1.5 Billion Anthropic A.I. Settlement
items.summary: The tech giant must pay $3,000 per pirated book that it used to train its chatbot. Many authors fear they could lose funds to others in the book business.

items.title: The Generation That’s Never Had to Say ‘Hello?’
items.summary: Now that there’s rarely any mystery to who’s calling, Gen Z has adopted a range of custom phone greetings — including no greeting at all.

items.title: F.B.I. Investigates Sale of Millions of Stolen Driver’s Licenses
items.summary: The blog Krebs on Security reported on an identity theft service trying to sell scans of licenses and other documents belonging to people in Canada and the United States.

items.title: Tumbler Ridge Shooting Survivors File 30 Lawsuits Against OpenAI
items.summary: The survivors contend that the company should have notified the police when it shut down the shooter’s disturbing ChatGPT account eight months before the February attack in British Columbia.
